overview: This 410-page file documents Japanese activities in Brazil from a 1944 arson investigation through postwar unrest, chiefly in São Paulo. Consular, FBI, Brazilian press, and Japanese community records trace Shindo Renmei’s denial of Japan’s surrender, associated threats and murders, and efforts to counter false victory claims through newspapers, films, broadcasts, and family correspondence. Later papers address a proposed Japanese envoy and the shipment of publications abroad.
interest: Shows how surrender denial fueled violence and how officials used newspapers, films, and family letters to challenge it.
